questions.q: What does `request.setHttpTimeout(10000)` accomplish in this lab's script?
options: Automatically retries the call up to 10 times
Converts the request from a GET into a POST
Bounds how long execute() waits for a response to 10 seconds, turning an indefinite hang into a failure the retry logic can react to
Sets the external system's rate limit to 10,000 requests per hour
questions.explain: setHttpTimeout is a real method that bounds the wait — without it, a hung connection never resolves into something the script can act on.

questions.q: Look at this condition: `if (!transportError && statusCode >= 400 && statusCode < 500) { ... return null; }`. Why does the script return without retrying here?
options: Because 4xx errors always resolve themselves after exactly one retry
Because gs.sleep() is not available for 4xx responses
A 4xx means the request itself is wrong, so an identical retry would just produce the identical wrong result
Because the external system is down and unreachable
questions.explain: Retrying a client error doesn't fix a malformed or unauthorized request — this is the non-retryable branch described in Lesson 20 and 21.

questions.q: Why does the script check `response.getErrorMessage()` in addition to `response.getStatusCode()`?
options: getErrorMessage() is required before getStatusCode() will return any value
A transport-level failure (host unreachable, connection timed out with no response) never produces a status code, so getErrorMessage() is needed to detect that case as retryable
Checking getErrorMessage() disables retries entirely
getErrorMessage() always returns the same value as getStatusCode()
questions.explain: RESTMessageV2 can fail at the transport level with no HTTP status code at all — getErrorMessage() is how the script catches that case.

questions.q: In the full retry loop, what happens to `backoffMs` between a failed attempt and the next one?
options: The script sleeps for backoffMs milliseconds, then doubles backoffMs before the next attempt, producing 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s delays
backoffMs stays fixed at 1000ms for every retry
backoffMs is reset to zero after every failed attempt
backoffMs is divided in half after every failed attempt
questions.explain: The gs.sleep(backoffMs) then backoffMs = backoffMs * 2 sequence is what implements exponential backoff rather than a fixed delay.

questions.q: Why does this lab's script log both a gs.warn() on each retryable failure and a final gs.error() if all attempts are exhausted?
options: Because gs.warn() automatically retries the call while gs.error() does not
So each individual attempt's status/transport detail is recorded as it happens, and a separate clear signal marks the point where retries ran out entirely for that city
Because gs.warn() and gs.error() write to completely unrelated, unconnected log tables
Because ServiceNow requires exactly two log calls per function or the script will not save
questions.explain: Logging each attempt's outcome plus a final exhaustion message gives a complete, readable trail of what was tried and how it ultimately ended.
